I farm 40 mu, and with only 2 people in the household I will keep the plan simple and steady. I will put 30 mu into my usual wheat-maize rotation and keep 10 mu in cotton. I have 30 years of experience, so I do not chase risky changes; I prefer stable yields and work I can manage myself. Because I have well irrigation, I will rely on irrigated wheat and maize as the backbone of income, and I will keep cotton on a smaller area because it takes more labor and more pesticide attention. For seed, I will use better-performing improved or hybrid types where they help yield and standability, but I will not overinvest. On fertilizer, I will feed wheat and maize a bit more because they are my main output crops, and I will keep potassium higher on cotton because that crop responds to it. For tillage, I will use rotary tillage for wheat, no-tillage for summer maize after wheat to save time and keep the season tight, and plough for cotton land so the soil is looser at planting. My target is not the highest possible yield; it is a dependable year with manageable labor, controlled cost, and stable production under local conditions in Quzhou County.
